1	\section{Monitoring, Telemetry, and Incident Response}
2	
3	\subsection{Telemetry Stack}
4	
5	部署的 Agent 每一次工具调用、每一条 API 输出都会被写入观测链路，流向三类系统：
6	
7	\begin{itemize}
8	    \item \textbf{Alerting}：基于 anomaly detection 设置阈值，如突发的自动化部署或高频 requests
9	    \item \textbf{Replay}：完整记录行为用于复现，包含 timeline、embeddings、输入/输出
10	    \item \textbf{Metrics}：自定义指标（alignment drift、policy deviation、human override rate）
11	\end{itemize}
12	
13	\begin{warningbox}{Observability isn't optional}
14	一旦 Agent 脱离常规模式，必须能够回放完整的调用链、看到 system prompt 以及外部 context。没有这个可视化，调查和治理几乎不可能。
15	\end{warningbox}
16	
17	\subsection{Incident Response Loop}
18	
19	当监控触发警报时，Anthropic 的响应流程包括：
20	
21	\begin{enumerate}
22	    \item 快速判定风险等级（green/orange/red）
23	    \item 自动切换至木偶式模式，所有输出需人工审批
24	    \item 开启 post-mortem，记录 timeline + root cause
25	    \item 更新 checklist 与 prompt 指令，防止 recurrence
26	\end{enumerate}
27	
28	\subsection{本章小结}
29	
30	Agent 监控需要 telemetry、alert、replay 三条腿支撑；一旦触发警报，组织必须以 structured loop（等级判定、containment、post-mortem、update）迅速响应，防止能力滑向风险区。
31	
32	\subsection{Data Pipelines and Instrumentation}
33	
34	Telemetry data is ingested into a multi-tier pipeline: real-time streaming, batch aggregation, and backing datastore for audit. Each agent interaction emits structured events with the following fields:
35	
36	\begin{itemize}
37	    \item `task\_id`, `agent\_variant`, `score`
38	    \item `tools\_used` list with duration/evidence per tool
39	    \item `alignment\_drift` delta vs baseline
40	    \item `human\_override` flag
41	\end{itemize}
42	
43	\begin{importantbox}{Why instrumentation matters}
44	Instrumentation not only powers alerts but also enables retrospective capability audits: you can slice by agent version, time window, tool set, or base capability and replay the exact logs that triggered a red flag.
45	\end{importantbox}
46	
47	The ingestion stack keeps both raw and derived layers. Raw events are immutable and tagged with `event\_hash` to ensure idempotency. Derived views pre-aggregate per ASL level and feed dashboards that teams monitor in daily standups.
48	
49	Dashboards themselves include `alignment drift`, `tool success`, `red-team exposure`, and `human override latency`. When any metric crosses thresholds, the telemetry system automatically tickets the incident response crew.
50	
51

1	\section{Metrics Glossary}
2	
3	\subsection{Key Capability Metrics}
4	
5	Anthropic tracks a catalog of capability metrics that feed into the evidence matrix. The main categories are:
6	
7	\begin{itemize}
8	    \item \textbf{Integrity}: factual accuracy, hallucination rate, citation precision
9	    \item \textbf{Autonomy}: plan depth, tool use depth, self-corrections
10	    \item \textbf{Control}: human override ratio, rollback events, command adherence
11	    \item \textbf{Impact}: productive output, decision quality, human satisfaction index
12	\end{itemize}
13	
14	Each metric is tied to a measurement method: `Integrity` uses reference corpora and automated fact-checkers, `Autonomy` uses action logs, `Control` uses human override logs, `Impact` uses structured surveys.
15	
16	\subsection{Glossary Table}
17	
18	\begin{tabular}{p{0.18\textwidth}p{0.22\textwidth}p{0.3\textwidth}p{0.22\textwidth}}
19	\toprule
20	Metric & Description & Data Source & Safety Threshold \\
21	\midrule
22	Fact Density & Share of claims verified by docs & embeddings + text diff & >82\% \\
23	Plan Completeness & Steps with dependency resolution & plan transcripts & no missing references \\
24	Tool Success & Tools used / tools invoked & telemetry logs & >95\% \\
25	Override Lag & Time between agent action and human override & workflow logs & >3 min to override \\
26	Drift Index & Deviation from baseline policy & alignment scores & <0.07 drift \\
27	Policy Noise & entropy in action selection & policy logs & <=0.3 \\
28	\bottomrule
29	\end{tabular}
30	
31	\begin{warningbox}{Metric calibration}
32	Metrics must be recalibrated when models change architecture, since scores are relative to behavior and can drift even if underlying capability remains stable.
33	\end{warningbox}
34	
35

<<<ES
\section{Monitoring, Telemetry, and Incident Response}

\subsection{Telemetry Stack}

Cada llamada a herramientas y cada salida de la API del agente desplegado se escriben en la cadena de observabilidad y fluyen hacia tres tipos de sistemas:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Alerting}: se configuran umbrales con base en anomaly detection, como despliegues automatizados repentinos o requests de alta frecuencia
    \item \textbf{Replay}: se registra el comportamiento completo para su reproducción, incluidos timeline, embeddings, entradas y salidas
    \item \textbf{Metrics}: métricas personalizadas (alignment drift, policy deviation, human override rate)
\end{itemize}

\begin{warningbox}{Observability isn't optional}
En cuanto el agente se desvía del modo habitual, debe ser posible reproducir la cadena de llamadas completa y ver el system prompt así como el context externo. Sin esta visibilidad, la investigación y la gobernanza son casi imposibles.
\end{warningbox}

\subsection{Incident Response Loop}

Cuando el monitoreo activa una alerta, el proceso de respuesta de Anthropic incluye:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item Se determina rápidamente el nivel de riesgo (green/orange/red)
    \item Se cambia automáticamente a un modo de marioneta, en el que toda salida requiere aprobación humana
    \item Se abre un post-mortem y se registran el timeline y la root cause
    \item Se actualizan el checklist y las instrucciones de prompt para evitar la recurrence
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{本章小结}

El monitoreo del agente necesita el sostén de tres elementos: telemetry, alert y replay; en cuanto se activa una alerta, la organización debe responder con rapidez mediante un structured loop (determinación del nivel, containment, post-mortem, update) para evitar que la capacidad se deslice hacia la zona de riesgo.

\subsection{Data Pipelines and Instrumentation}

Telemetry data is ingested into a multi-tier pipeline: real-time streaming, batch aggregation, and backing datastore for audit. Each agent interaction emits structured events with the following fields:

\begin{itemize}
    \item `task\_id`, `agent\_variant`, `score`
    \item `tools\_used` list with duration/evidence per tool
    \item `alignment\_drift` delta vs baseline
    \item `human\_override` flag
\end{itemize}

\begin{importantbox}{Why instrumentation matters}
Instrumentation not only powers alerts but also enables retrospective capability audits: you can slice by agent version, time window, tool set, or base capability and replay the exact logs that triggered a red flag.
\end{importantbox}

The ingestion stack keeps both raw and derived layers. Raw events are immutable and tagged with `event\_hash` to ensure idempotency. Derived views pre-aggregate per ASL level and feed dashboards that teams monitor in daily standups.

Dashboards themselves include `alignment drift`, `tool success`, `red-team exposure`, and `human override latency`. When any metric crosses thresholds, the telemetry system automatically tickets the incident response crew.

ES>>>
